text: Updates on my research and expository papers, discussion of open problems, and other maths-related topics. By Terence Tao 24 October, 2026 in advertising | Tags: Abhinav Nellore , Johannes Schmitt , Rachel Ward , Soledad Villar | by Terence Tao [This is a guest post by Abhinav Nellore , Johannes Schmitt , Soledad Villar , and Rachel Ward – T.] OpenAI’s math write-ups at https://github.com/openai/math can be difficult to understand and can have incomplete citations. https://github.com/mathcommunity/oai-math-revised/ seeks to be an inclusive effort to improve these write-ups, and the broader math community–students, postdocs, professors, and enthusiasts–is invited to participate. The repo is browsable at https://mathcommunity.github.io/oai-math-revised/ We also invite the community to email mathcommunityadmin@gmail.com if they want to serve as admins/reviewers and for which categories from https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/overview.pdf they’d be appropriate for reviews. Comments feed for this article 24 October, 2026 at 10:01 am Anonymous So it is up to unpaid volunteers to sift through OpenAI’s slop and refine their output for them? After all the fanciful debate about putting pressure on these trillion-dollar companies, nothing has fundamentally shifted in our approach? It’s good to know that you can always count on academia to never change for the better even in the face of the most extreme circumstances. 24 October, 2026 at 10:17 am Skip Tich Given the nature of the existing tension between the mathematical community and frontier labs, I have to wonder, is this really the right thing to do? To engage with the labs in good faith, cleaning up and polishing their results for them? It seems that this will mainly serve to validate the approach that OpenAI has taken, and to pigeonhole mathematicians into the role of interpreting the “gifts” the “machine gods” have bestowed upon us, further distracting them from what should be their main purpose right now, which is figuring out how to act autonomously as a community going forward. In addition, these improved writeups will be used as training data for the future models. OpenAI will eat these up and spit you out without so much as a thank you. 24 October, 2026 at 10:27 am Anonymous Several of the authors appear to be heavily involved in machine learning and AI for math. While it is expected that initiatives would come from such a direction, it is not really a neutral organization. The repository is separate from OpenAI, but participants will work for free for OpenAI. 24 October, 2026 at 10:35 am Lior Silberman Why is it our job to revise OpenAI’s manuscripts? They are the authors and they are responsible for the content and the quality of the writing. We are interested in understanding the scientific advance, regardless of the source, and we are fully within our rights to produce review articles and share our understanding, but it seems weird for me to spend volunteer efforts into improving write-ups that belong to a wealthy for-profit company. If they want these services they should pay for them.
